Title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Sexual Health Services
Reference: F/109/SHS/26/SB
Buying organisation: COUNTESS OF CHESTER HOSPITAL NHS FOUNDATION TRUST
Published: 2026-11-18
Closing: 2027-01-14
Procurement category: services
Classification: Health services
Description: The demand for accessible, high-quality and innovative sexual health services continues to evolve in response to changing population needs, advances in clinical practice, increasing digital delivery models and the ongoing focus on reducing health inequalities. The Framework will provide Relevant Authorities with a fully compliant route for the provision of sexual health services, supporting the commissioning of integrated, digital, clinical, diagnostic, prevention, outreach and specialist support services. The Framework is designed to enable Contracting Authorities to secure services that improve public health outcomes, promote early intervention and prevention, support vulnerable populations, and ensure equitable access to care. The overall aim of the Framework is to provide a compliant
title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Sexual Health Services

text:
Title: Provision of a Medical Advisory Service for Scottish Public Pension Agency
Reference: SPPA/2030-03/2026/057
Buying organisation: Scottish Public Pensions Agency
Published: 2026-11-18
Closing: 2027-01-06
Procurement category: services
Classification: Health and social work services
Description: Provision of a Medical Advisory Service to support the Contracting Authority’s activities in administering the National Health Service (NHS) and Teachers’ pension schemes in Scotland and determining the Local Government Pension Scheme (Scotland)’s (LGPS) Internal Disputes Resolution Procedure (IDRP)’s appeals. For the period 01 April 2027 to 31 March 2030. The Contracting Authority may, by giving notice to the Economic Operator, extend the period of the contract to a date falling no later than 31 March 2032. Subject to that constraint, the Contracting Authority may extend the period of the Contract on more than one occasion.
title: Provision of a Medical Advisory Service for Scottish Public Pension Agency

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Council of the Royal Borough of Greenwich (hereinafter referred to as “the Council”) proposes to make the above-mentioned Orders under sections 6, 45, 46, 49, 124 and Part IV of Schedule 9 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, as amended. 2. The general effect of the Orders would be to: a) to replace 2.5 metres to 3 metres of various existing control where appropriate with a secure bicycle parking facility (cycle hangar) in each of the following locations: i. Allenby Road, north-east side, from a point 16.95 metres south-east of the south-eastern building line of No.2 Allenby Road in a north-westerly direction replacing ‘No waiting at any time’ restrictions; Annandale Road, west side, from a point 6 metres south of the southern property boundary of No. 85 Annandale Road in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Residents and Business Permit Holders Only Mon-Fri 9am-6.30pm Zone W’ bay; Bowater Place, east side, from a point 5 metres south of the southern property boundary of No. 2 Bowater Place in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Free Parking Place’ restriction; Bramhope Lane, east side, from a point 4.5 metres south of the northern building line of Victor House in a northerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Free Parking Place’; Calydon Road, north-west side, from a point 4 metres south-west of the common boundary of Nos. 11 and 13 Calydon Road in a north-easterly direction replacing ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm’ restrictions; Church Manorway, east side, from a point 11.8 metres south of the southern building line of No.2 Church Manorway in a northerly direction, replacing ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm’ restrictions; Deptford Green, west side, from a point 5.1 metres south of its junction with Borthwick Street in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Limited Waiting 1 Hour No Return 30 Mins Mon-Fri 12pm-2pm’ bay; Earlswood Street, north-east side, from a point 7.8 metres north-west of the north-western property boundary of No. 27 Earlswood Street in a north-westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders Only 9am-6.30pm Zone EG’ bay; Egerton Drive, west side, from a point 5.8 metres south of its junction with Ashburnham Place in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Residents and Business Permit Holders Only Mon-Sat 9am-5pm and Sun 9am-6pm Zone G’ restrictions; Eversley Road, south side, from a point 14.65 metres west of the eastern property boundary of No. 19 Wyndcliff Road in an easterly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone C’ bay; Eversley Road, south side, from a point 14.5 metres west of the western building line of No.2 Eversley Road in a westerly direction, replacing ‘No waiting at any time’ restrictions; Grangehill Road, south-west side, from a point 22 metres north-west of its junction with Greenvale Road in a north-westerly direction, replacing ‘Free Parking Place’ and ‘No Waiting Mon-Fri 11am-12.30pm’ restrictions; Gurdon Road, south side, from a point 8.9 metres west of the eastern property boundary of No. 30 Dupree Road in a westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone C’ bay; Humber Road, north-west side, from a point 14 metres south-west of the south-western property boundary of No. 55 Humber Road in a south-westerly direction, replacing ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm’ and ‘Cycle Hire Parking Place’ restrictions; Kirkside Road, south side, from a point 3.5 metres west of the common boundary of Nos. 37 and 39 Kirkside Road in an easterly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone W’ bay; Lyveden Road, north side, from a point 6.9 metres west of its junction with Furzefield Road in a westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone C’ bay; Owenite Street, west side, from a point 11.65 metres north of the northern property boundary of No.2 Owenite Street in a northerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders Only Mon-Fri 11am-1pm Zone AW’ bay; Point Hill, south-west side, from a point 12.4 metres north of the northern kerbline of Point Close for 3 metres in a northerly direction replacing ‘No waiting at any time’ restrictions and part of a ‘Cycle Hire Parking Place’; The Heights, north side, from a point 6.6 metres west of the eastern building line of No. 27a and 27b The Heights in a westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Free Parking Place’ and ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm’

Transport for London, hereby gives notice that it intends to make the above named Order under section 6 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984. 2. The general nature and effect of the Order will be to: (1) shorten the 30 metre long Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm parking 30 minute No return 1 hour bay outside Nos. 13 to 23 Lewisham Road by 14 metres to accommodate an 11.5 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay bracketed by 1.2 metre traffic islands at each end. A double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be introduced to accommodate the change; (2) shorten the 16 metre long Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the north-eastern kerb of Arbroath Road outside Nos. 179 and 181 Well Hall Road by 10.5 metres to accommodate an 8.2 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.4 metre traffic islands at its north-western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (3) replace the Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm Parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the western kerb of Cobbett Road at the side of St Barnabas Church, Rochester Way, with a 12 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic islands at its southern end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (4) replace the Parking at Any Time bay at the northern kerb of Dickson Road at the side of No. 125 Well Hall Road with an 8 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic islands at its western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (5) shorten the 17 metre long Monday to Saturday 10am to 4pm loading 20 mins No return 40 minutes and Disabled Persons’ Vehicles 3 hours bay at the north-eastern kerb of Dunblane Road outside No. 369 Well Hall Road by 10.4 metres to accommodate an 9 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.4 metre traffic islands its north-western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (6) replace the Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm Parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the north-eastern kerb of Legatt Road, at the side of No. 515 Westhorne Avenue, with a 9 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic island at its north-western end. A double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be introduced to accommodate the change; (7) replace the Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm Parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the southern kerb of side road Well Hall Road, opposite No. 171 Well Hall Road, with a 9 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic island at its western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (8) make administrative changes to the controls on the Side Road Well Hall Road to correct historical errors. 3. The roads which would be affected by the Order are the A2 GLA side road Lewisham Road, the A205 GLA side roads Arbroath Road, Cobbett Road, Dickson Road, Dunblane Road, Legatt Road and Well Hall Road. 4. A copy of the Order, a statement of Transport for London’s reasons for the proposals, a map indicating the location and effect of the Order and copies of any Order revoked, suspended or varied by the Order can be inspected by visiting our website at https://haveyoursay.tfl.gov.uk/tro and selecting the relevant borough and reference the Traffic Order relates to or by appointment during normal office hours at our office at the address below. To arrange an appointment please email [contact removed] Copies of the documents may be requested via email at [contact removed], or by post at the following address quoting reference SNO/REGULATION/STOT/GK/TRO/GLA/2026/0650: • Transport for London, Streets Traffic Order Team (SNO/REGULATION/STOT), Palestra, 197 Blackfriars Road, London, SE1 8NJ. 5. All objections and other representations to the proposed Order must be made in writing and must specify the grounds on which they are made. Objections and representations must be sent to Transport for London, Streets Traffic Order Team, Palestra, 197 Blackfriars Road, London, SE1 8NJ or by emailing [contact removed] quoting reference SNO/REGULATION/STOT/GK/TRO/GLA/2026/0650, to arrive before 9th December 2026. Please note due to hybrid working access to post is restricted and requests for documents and confirmation of your objections or representations may be delayed. Objections and other representations may be communicated to other persons who may be affected. Dated this 18th day of November

Install 'at any time' waiting restrictions in sections of roads as set out in the Schedule to this notice below. 2. Install blue badge disabled parking bays at the following locations: i) Outside No. 112 Hartland Drive, Ruislip ii) Outside Nos. 15/19/23 Portland Road, Hayes iii) Alongside No. 100A Bedford Avenue, Hayes 3. Remove the redundant blue badge disabled parking bays at the following locations: i) Outside No. 45 Cranford Lane, Hayes (convert to Zone H1 permit holder parking place). ii) Outside No. 144 Waltham Avenue, Hayes iii) Outside No. 159 Tudor Road, Hayes iv) Outside No. 75 Great Central Avenue, Ruislip v) Outside No. 73 Great Central Avenue, Ruislip 4. Further information can be obtained by email [contact removed] . If you wish to comment on, or object to the proposals please write or email by 9th December 2026, stating grounds for objection and your home address to Transport & Projects, Residents Services, Civic Centre, Uxbridge, Middlesex UB8 1UW quoting reference 3N/04/18/11/26. Dated this the 18th day of November 2026. GLOVERS GROVE, RUISLIP – Opposite the junction with Greystoke Drive. HIGHLAND ROAD, NORTHWOOD – At the junction with Cranbourne Road. CRANBOURNE ROAD, NORTHWOOD – At the junction with Highland Road. NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that Westminster City Council on 16th November 2026 made the above Order under sections 6, 45, 46, 49, 63 and 124 of and Part IV of Schedule 9 to the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, as amended. 2. The general effect of the Order will be, in connection with improvements to the cycle routes on Lupus Street, to: (a) replace the residents’ parking place on the west side of Lupus Street, between Turpentine Lane and Westmoreland Terrace, with double yellow line “at any time” waiting restrictions; (b) introduce double yellow line “at any time” waiting restrictions on both sides of Lupus Street, on the bend opposite Westmoreland Terrace and Sussex Street; (c) replace the redundant doctor parking place on the south side of Lupus Street, outside Nash House, with a car club parking place; (d) relocate the cycle hangar and one electric vehicle parking bay from the north side of Lupus Street, at the rear of No. 96 Gloucester Street, to the south side of Lupus Street, outside Nash House (replacing the car club parking place); and (e) introduce a loading bay (operating between 7.00 a.m. and 7.00 p.m. throughout the week, with a maximum stay of 2 hours and no return within 1 hour) on the south side of Lupus Street, outside De Quincey House (replacing two pay-by-phone parking bays and a length of single yellow line waiting restrictions). An advisory with-flow cycle lane will also be introduced on the north side of Lupus Street, between Turpentine Lane and Westmoreland Terrace. 3. The Order, which will come into force on 23rd November 2026, and other documents giving more detailed particulars of the Order are available for inspection until 28th December 2026 at https://westminstertransportationservices.co.uk/notices and, in person by appointment only, at Westminster City Hall, 64 Victoria Street, London, SW1E 6QP, between 9.00 a.m. and 5.00 p.m. on Mondays to Fridays (except bank / public holidays). Please telephone 020 3116 9388 or email [contact removed] to arrange an appointment. 4. Any person desiring to question the validity of the Order or of any provision contained therein on the grounds that it is not within the relevant powers of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 or that any of the relevant requirements thereof or of any relevant regulations made thereunder have not been complied with in relation to the Order may, within six weeks from the date on which the Order was made, make application for the purpose to the High Court. Dated 18th November 2026 JONATHAN ROWING, Head of Parking (The officer appointed for this purpose) Actions Save notice to My Gazette Remove from My Gazette Loading... NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham will make the above-mentioned Orders under the powers granted by sections 6, 32, 35, 45, 46, 49 and 124 of, and Part IV of Schedule 9 to, the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 (as amended). 2. The general effect of the above-mentioned Order which comes into operation on the 25th November 2026 will be to Ebike Hire Bays at the following: 1. Ashchurch Park Villas - opposite 24 Ashchurch Park Villas, including 1 metre extension of southern end of double yellow lines at the northwest side of 14 Ashchurch Terrace. 2. Barclay Road – outside 613a Fuham Road 3. Black Lion Lane – on the west side junction with King Street 4. Britannia Road – on the west side junction with Fulham Road. 5. Clancarty Road – opposite 80 to 82 with a 1 metre double yellow line installed opposite 84 6. Daisy Lane – on the eastern side junction with Peterborough Road. 7. Darlan Road – on the northern side at the junction with Fulham Road. 8. Hurlingham Road – opposite 68 to 66 9. Maxwell Road – on the south side junction with Kings Road, including 1 metre double yellow line installed adjacent at the southeastern side of bay. 10. Merrington Road – on the northern side by the junction with Seagrave Road, adjacent to cycle hanger. 11. Michael Road – on the southern side by the junction with Sands End Lane, adjacent to cycle hire station 12. Ongar Road – on the west side junction with Lillie Road. 13. Ravenscourt Gardens – opposite 2F to 2E 14. Rigault Road – at the western side of 1 Jubilee Terrace. 15. Rylett Crescent – at the western side of 35 Binden Road by the junction, including 1 metre extension of southern end of double yellow lines at the junction with Binden Road. 16. Sawley Road – on the south side junction with Sedgeford Road with a 1.8 metre extension of southern side double yellow line at the junction with Sedgeford Road. 17. Sawley Road (2) – opposite 45 to 47 18. Sedlescombe Road – on the southern side at the junction with Ongar Road and conversion of single yellow line at the junction with Ongar Road to a double yellow line 19. Walham Grove – outside 60 20. Wendell Road – opposite 67 21. Wulfstan Street – on the south side by the junction with Du Cane Road. 22. To make further amendments to bring the Map-Based Orders in line with the on-street layout. 3. A copy of the Orders, the Statement of Reasons for proposing to make the Orders, and documents giving more detailed particulars can be inspected, by appointment, during normal office hours on Mondays to Fridays inclusive until the end of a period of 6 weeks beginning with the date on which the Orders are made, or as the case may be, the Council decides not to make the Orders. 4. If any person wishes to question the validity of the Order or any of the provisions on the grounds that it or they are not within the powers conferred by the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, or that any requirement of that Act or of any instrument made under that Act has not been complied with, that person may, within 6 weeks from the date on which the Order is made, apply for the purpose to the High Court may write to the Transport and Highways Department, Environmental Services, Town Hall Extension, King Street, Hammersmith, W6 9JU or via email to [contact removed] Dated 18th November 2026 John Galsworthy, Director of Climate Change and Transport Public Realm Actions Save notice to My Gazette Remove from My Gazette Loading... NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Council of the London Borough of Newham on 16 November 2026 made the above-mentioned Order under Section 9 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 “the Act”, as amended. 2. The effect of the Order will be to extend the operational hours of the permit-holder parking bays in Snowshill Road from the current 9am to 5pm, Monday to Saturday to being operational from 9am to 10pm on all days. 3. Further information may be obtained by telephoning 020 8430 2000. 4. The Experimental Order, which will come into force on 30 November 2026, a plan and other documents giving more detailed particulars of the Order are available for inspection by appointment during normal office hours on Monday to Friday inclusive at Newham Dockside, 1000 Dockside Road E16 2QU, by telephoning 020 3373 6415 or by emailing [contact removed] until such time as the Orders cease to have effect. 5. If any person wishes to question the validity of the Order or of any of its provisions on the grounds that it or they are not within the powers conferred by the Act, or that any requirement of the Act or of any instrument made under the Act has not been complied with, that person may, within six weeks from the date on which the Orders are made, apply for the purpose to the High Court. 6. If the provisions of the Order continue in force for a period of not less than six months, the Council will be considering in due course whether the provisions of the experimental Order and other measures should be continued in force indefinitely by means of Orders under Section 6 of the said Act of 1984. 7. Within a period of six months – (a) beginning with the day on which the experimental Order came into force; or (b) if the Order is varied by another Order or modified pursuant to Section 10(2) of the 1984 Act, beginning with the day on which the variation or modification or the latest variation or modification came into force; any person may object to the making of the Order for the purpose of such indefinite continuation. 8. All objections and other representations relating to the continuation of the Order must be made in writing. All objections must specify the grounds on which they are made. They should be sent to the Director of Highways, Parking & Transportation, London Borough of Newham, 3rd Floor West, Newham Dockside, 1000 Dockside Road, London E16 2QU or by email, quoting the Order title, to: [contact removed] 9. Under the requirements of current access to information legislation, any letter or e-mail sent to the Council in response to this Notice may be subject to publication or disclosure, or both, including communication to other persons affected. Dated 18 November 2026 Dhiresh Bhatt, Director of Highways, Parking & Transportation Actions Save notice to My Gazette Remove from My Gazette Loading... The Council of the Royal Borough of Greenwich hereby gives notice that it intends to make an Order to restrict vehicles from waiting or loading in Stane Way to facilitate the safe movement of construction vehicles whilst building works are carried out. 2. The effect of the Order would be to provide double yellow lines ‘at any time’ waiting restriction and double kerb blips ‘at any time’ loading restriction in: a) Stane Way: i. (west and north-west side) between its westernmost extremity and a point opposite the northeastern wall of No.1 (for the entire length of that which is publicly maintained); ii. Nothing in this Notice will apply to anything done with the permission or at the direction of a police constable in uniform or traffic warden, to emergency vehicles or service vehicles. 4. The Order would come into force on 25th November 2026 and would be valid for a maximum period of 18 months or until the works have been completed, whichever is the sooner. 5. Queries concerning these works should be directed to [contact removed] quoting reference TT10(26) Stane Way Temp Restrictions. NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Council of the Royal Borough of Greenwich proposes to make the above-mentioned Order under Sections 6, 22C and 22D of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 (RTRA 1984), as amended. 2. The general effect of the Order would be to make permanent the existing temporary ATTRO operating in the vicinity of The Valley stadium, that was made on 6th August 2025 under Section 14(1) by virtue of sections 22C and 22D of the RTRA 1984, and to continue the provision of that Order which was: To prohibit all vehicles and pedestrians, as required, from entering, exiting or proceeding in the roads (including footpaths, footways, cycle routes, byways and roads other than those for which a given traffic authority is responsible) during specified times or as required on event days, when intelligence dictates or the threat level is sufficient to require additional restrictions upon traffic movements (for football or other sporting events these closures will be 2 hours in advance of the published start time and ending 1 hour after conclusion of said event (or when safe to do so)), at the locations listed below: a. Delafield Road from the east side of its junction with Swallowfield Road (outside no. 77 Delafield Road) to its junction with Charlton Church Lane; b. Charlton Church Lane from its junction with A206 Woolwich Road to the north side of its junction with Nadine Street (outside no. 85 Charlton Church Lane); c. Floyd Road (entire length); d. Valley Grove (entire length); e. Harvey Gardens from its junction with Floyd Road/Ransom Road to its junction with Charlton Lane (through section adjacent to The Valley Football Stadium only); f. Charlton Lane from the north side of its junction with Harvey Gardens (outside no. 94 Charlton Lane) to the south side of its junction with Lansdowne Mews (outside No.148a Charlton Lane). 3. None of the prohibitions in item 2 of this Notice would apply to: a. any vehicle when used for fire brigade, ambulance or police purposes; b. anything done with the permission or at the direction of a police constable in uniform, and authorised agent or designated. 4. Copies of the proposed Orders and other relevant documents can be inspected during normal office hours on Mondays to Fridays inclusive at the Woolwich Centre Library, The Woolwich Centre, 35 Wellington Street, London SE18 6HQ. 5. Any person who wishes to object to the proposals or make other representations should send a statement in writing quoting reference ‘T22(26) Valley Stadium ATTRO’ by 9th December 2026 to: Parking Design Team, 3rd Floor, The Woolwich Centre, 35 Wellington Street, London SE18 6HQ or [contact removed] Please note all objections or comments must specify the grounds on which they are made. Dated 18th November 2026 Ryan Nibbs, Assistant Director of Transportation Actions Save notice to My Gazette Remove from My Gazette Loading... Note: The Insolvency Service considers that notice cannot be given under this rule prior to liquidation unless there is an office holder acting in relation to the company as administrator, administrative receiver or supervisor of a CVA. NOTICE TO THE CREDITORS OF AN INSOLVENT COMPANY REGARDING THE RE-USE OF A PROHIBITED NAME RULE 22.4 OF THE INSOLVENCY (ENGLAND AND WALES) RULES 2016 COLOUR GRAPHICS LTD Registered Number: 04794437 Trading Name: Trading name or style: Colour Graphics / Fabrix Registered office: Azzurri House, Walsall Road, Aldridge, Walsall, WS9 0RB Principal trading address: Azzurri House, Walsall Road, Aldridge, Walsall, WS9 0RB On 15 October 2026 the above-named company went into insolvent liquidation. I, James Birch of 1 Heath Gap, Lichfield, WS13 8PH, was a director of the above-named company during the 12 months ending with the day before it went into liquidation. I give notice that it is my intention to act in all or any of the ways specified in section 216(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 in connection with, or for the purposes of, the carrying on of the whole or substantially the whole of the business of the insolvent company under the following name: Printcorp Ltd t/a Colour Graphics; Printcorp Ltd t/a Fabrix. Rule 22.5 - Statement as to the effect of the notice under rule 22.4(2): “Section 216(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 lists the activities that a director of a company that has gone into insolvent liquidation may not undertake unless the court gives permission or there is an exception in the Insolvency Rules made under the Insolvency Act 1986. (This includes the exceptions in Part 22 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016). These activities are- (a) acting as a director of another company that is known by a name which is either the same as a name used by the company in insolvent liquidation in the 12 months before it entered liquidation or is so similar as to suggest an association with that company; (b) directly or indirectly being concerned or taking part in the promotion, formation or management of any such company; or (c) directly or indirectly being concerned in the carrying on of a business otherwise than through a company under a name of the kind mentioned in (a) above. This notice is given under rule 22.4 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016 where the business of a company which is in, or may go into, insolvent liquidation is, or is to be, carried on otherwise than by the company in liquidation with the involvement of a director of that company and under the same or a similar name to that of that company. The purpose of the giving of this notice is to permit the director to act in these circumstances where the company enters (or has entered) insolvent liquidation without the director committing a criminal offence and in the case of the carrying on of the business through another company, being personally liable for that company’s debts. Notice may be given where the person giving the notice is already the director of a company which proposes to adopt a prohibited name.” Notes: 1. This notice must be given to every creditor of the insolvent company whose name and address is known or is ascertainable on the making of such enquiries as are reasonable in the circumstances. 2. This notice must be published in the London Gazette. 3. The notice to creditors and the London Gazette must be given and published no later than 28 days after completion of the acquisition of the whole (or substantially the whole) of the business of the insolvent company under arrangements made by the liquidator or office holder acting as administrator, administrative receiver or supervisor of a CVA. text: Gareth Davies Appointed as New Home Office Permanent Secretary | Gareth is currently Permanent Secretary at the Department for Business and Trade. He has previously held senior roles across government in business, transport and Downing Street. He started his career in the private sector, and has worked across Europe and south east Asia. Gareth set up the Department for Business and Trade and has led it over the last three years. During this time, the department secured major trade deals including with India and the United States, landed major investments, hosted the International Investment Summit, launched the Industrial Strategy, and passed the Employment Rights Act. Home Secretary, the Rt Hon Shabana Mahmood MP, said: Gareth Davies brings decades of experience in senior government and private sector roles, and a strong record of delivery supporting British trade and industry and transforming departments. I look forward to working with Gareth as we drive forward the most significant reforms to policing and migration in generations, and deliver our mission to keep the British public safe and restore order to our borders. I would also like to thank Dame Antonia Romeo for her exceptional leadership of the department, and Simon Ridley for his valuable counsel while serving as Acting Permanent Secretary in recent months. Cabinet Secretary, Dame Antonia Romeo, said: This is an important appointment for the Home Office and the Civil Service. Gareth is a brilliant permanent secretary who brings a wealth of experience of delivery and innovation from the public and private sectors. The Home Office is charged with delivery of some of the Government’s highest priorities, and Gareth is strongly suited to grip delivery and productivity in support of the Home Secretary and the Prime Minister. I would also like to thank Simon Ridley for his strong leadership of the department in the interim period. Gareth Davies CB said: It’s an honour to be appointed Permanent Secretary of the Home Office - one of the great offices of state. There’s no more important agenda in government than keeping the country safe and secure. I’m looking forward to working with the amazing team of civil servants to deliver the Home Secretary’s priorities and build a department that is even more innovative and productive. I would like to thank the incredible team at the Department of Business and Trade. They should be very proud of the difference they make to the lives of families and communities across our country. The appointment has been agreed by the First Civil Service Commissioner and the Prime Minister. Gareth Davies will start as Home Office Permanent Secretary on the 6th April. Amanda Brooks CBE has been appointed Interim Permanent Secretary at the Department for Business and Trade. Amanda is currently Director General for Trade at the Department and has a wealth of experience in senior government roles covering domestic and international economic policy.
title: Gareth Davies Appointed as New Home Office Permanent Secretary

text: Tom Riordan Appointed as New Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government | The Cabinet Secretary, with the approval of the Prime Minister, has appointed Tom Riordan as the new Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG). Tom is currently the Northern Growth Envoy. He has previously been Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Operating Officer at the Department of Health and Social Care, and before that was Chief Executive of Leeds City Council. Angela Rayner, Secretary of State for Housing, Communities & Local Government, said: Few people have done more than Tom Riordan to champion devolution, good growth and strong local leadership - which makes him the perfect appointment at a critical time. I’m delighted he’s joining MHCLG and look forward to working with him as we get on with building the homes we need, improving local places and giving communities more control over their future. I’d also like to thank Dame Sarah Healey for her leadership of the department and Will Garton for his support as Interim Permanent Secretary in recent months. Cabinet Secretary, Dame Antonia Romeo, said: I am delighted to announce Tom’s appointment as Permanent Secretary for MHCLG. Tom’s wealth of experience in central and local government, combined with his time as the Northern Growth Envoy and CEO of Leeds City Council, makes him ideally suited to lead MHCLG’s crucial policy agenda delivering devolution and growth in every postcode. I would also like to thank Will Garton for his leadership of the department in the interim period. Tom Riordan said: It’s a privilege to be taking up such an important job to help ensure the whole country benefits from more affordable and safe homes, well run public services and strong regional growth. This feels like the right job at the right time as the Government devolves power, given how much I’ve valued working in local and regional government, and applying that learning to improving national policy. The appointment follows an internal recruitment exercise chaired by the independent First Civil Service Commissioner. Tom will start as MHCLG Permanent Secretary on 21 September. ENDS Notes to Editors: This is a Permanent Secretary level appointment, offered on a fixed term basis for five years. Tom is currently Northern Growth Envoy, based in HM Treasury. Prior to that he was Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Operating Officer at DHSC and was CEO of Leeds City Council between 2010 and 2024.
title: Tom Riordan Appointed as New Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

text: Clara Swinson appointed as Second Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Justice | The appointment has been made with the approval of the Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister. Her appointment is part of the government’s plan to reform the justice system. As Second Permanent Secretary, she will provide leadership across the Criminal Justice System in taking forward the government’s response to Sir Brian Leveson’s Independent Review of the Criminal Courts. Clara is currently Second Permanent Secretary in the Cabinet Office. The Secretary of State for Justice and the Deputy Prime Minister, the Rt Hon. David Lammy said: I am pleased that Clara Swinson is joining the Ministry of Justice bringing her extensive experience to this role. I look forward to working with Clara to deliver our plan for faster and fairer justice for victims by combining investment, reform, and modernisation. Permanent Secretary MOJ, Dr Jo Farrar said: I am delighted to welcome Clara to the Ministry of Justice. Clara brings a wealth of experience, of working across systems, both from her current role in the Cabinet Office and her time at the Department of Health and Social Care. I look forward to working with her in the Ministry of Justice. Clara Swinson said: I am very pleased to be joining the Ministry of Justice at such a critical time and taking forward the government’s response to Sir Brian Leveson’s important recommendations for the criminal justice system. Clara will take up her new post in April 2026.
title: Clara Swinson appointed as Second Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Justice

I, Marshall Lee of c/o Unit 5B, Lyne Mushroom Farm, Longcross Road, Chertsey, Surrey, KT16 0DH, was a director of the above-named company during the 12 months ending with the day before it went into liquidation. I give notice that it is my intention to act in one or more of the ways specified in section 216(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 in connection with, or for the purposes of, the carrying on of the whole or substantially the whole of the business of the insolvent company under the following name: Performance Automotive Parts Ltd T/A ML Performance I would not otherwise be permitted to undertake those activities without the leave of the court or the application of an exception created by Rules made under the Insolvency Act 1986. Breach of the prohibition created by section 216 of The Insolvency Act 1986 is a criminal offence. Rule 22.5 - Statement as to the effect of the notice under rule 22.4(2): Section 216(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 lists the activities that a director of a company that has gone into insolvent liquidation may not undertake unless the court gives permission or there is an exception in the Insolvency Rules made under the Insolvency Act 1986. (This includes the exceptions in Part 22 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016.) These activities are- (a) acting as a director of another company that is known by a name which is either the same as a name used by the company in insolvent liquidation in the 12 months before it entered liquidation or is so similar as to suggest an association with that company; (b) directly or indirectly being concerned or taking part in the promotion, formation or management of any such company; or (c) directly or indirectly being concerned in the carrying on of a business otherwise than through a company under a name of the kind mentioned in (a) above. This notice is given under rule 22.4 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016 where the business of a company which is in, or may go into, insolvent liquidation is, or is to be, carried on otherwise than by the company in liquidation with the involvement of a director of that company and under the same or a similar name to that of that company. The purpose of giving this notice is to permit the director to act in these circumstances where the company enters (or has entered) insolvent liquidation without the director committing a criminal offence and in the case of the carrying on of the business through another company, being personally liable for that company`s debts. Notice may be given where the person giving the notice is already the director of a company which proposes to adopt a prohibited name. Notice timeline (09676118) Loading... Rule 22.5 - Statement as to the effect of the notice under rule 22.4(2): Section 216(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 lists the activities that a director of a company that has gone into insolvent liquidation may not undertake unless the court gives permission or there is an exception in the Insolvency Rules made under the Insolvency Act 1986. (This includes the exceptions in Part 22 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016.) These activities are - (a) acting as a director of another company that is known by a name which is either the same as a name used by the company in insolvent liquidation in the 12 months before it entered liquidation or is so similar as to suggest an association with that company; (b) directly or indirectly being concerned or taking part in the promotion, formation or management of any such company; or (c) directly or indirectly being concerned in the carrying on of a business otherwise than through a company under a name of the kind mentioned in (a) above. This notice is given under rule 22.4 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016 where the business of a company which is in, or may go into, insolvent liquidation is, or is to be, carried on otherwise than by the company in liquidation with the involvement of a director of that company and under the same or a similar name to that of that company. The purpose of giving this notice is to permit the director to act in these circumstances where the company enters (or has entered) insolvent liquidation without the director committing a criminal offence and in the case of the carrying on of the business through another company, being personally liable for that company`s debts. Notice may be given where the person giving the notice is already the director of a company which proposes to adopt a prohibited name. Notice timeline (02395203) Loading... The crossing will incorporate a controlled area indicated by zig-zag markings along the carriageway where parking and loading will be prohibited at all times in the length of road specified in the schedule to this Notice. SCHEDULE – ZEBRA PEDESTRIAN CROSSING & CENTRE REFUGE South Eden Park Road (both sides) • from its junction with Creswell Drive in a south-westerly and southerly direction for an approximate distance of 28 metres Statement of the Council’s Reasons The existing uncontrolled crossing is being upgraded to include a Zebra pedestrian crossing with a centre refuge to facilitate the passage of pedestrians, including blind and partially sighted individuals in navigating them safely across South Eden Park Road. It also aims to avoid danger to persons or other traffic using the road and prevents the likelihood of any such dangers arising, recognising the route is highly used by students attending nearby schools in the area. NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Council of the Royal Borough of Greenwich on 20 November 2026 made the above-mentioned Order under sections 6, 35, 45, 46, 49 and 124 of and part IV of Schedule 9 to the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, as amended. The Order will come into force on 2 December 2026. 2. The general effect of the Order is to provide parking controls as shown within those lengths of housing estate road detailed below:- Edge Hill - To introduce double yellow line no waiting at any time restrictions along the front of garages of the block numbered 38-156 Edge Hill. Geoffrey Covey House, Gilbourne Estate – This is a new build on Housing land with a proposal for one single disabled bay. Glyndon Estate, Invermore Place – (Estate Zone HE09 Permit Holders) - To convert a parking bay into a disabled bay. Lemmon Road – (Estate Zone HW08 Permit Holders) - To convert two parking bays into disabled bays. Marshland House, Dahlia Road – To provide 7 disabled spaces and no waiting at any time restrictions. Milnes Estate, at Rutland House - To convert an existing parking bay into a disabled bay for a disabled resident. Rideout Street, at Murray House (Estate Zone HC27 Permit Holders) - To convert an existing parking bay into a disabled bay for a disabled resident at Murray House. Note: the proposal advertised on 19th August 2026 in Prior Street Garages - to introduce double yellow line no waiting at any time restrictions, no loading and unloading restrictions and one loading bay with maximum stay of 40 minutes at the rear of 38-42 Prior Street, has been deferred and at a future time will be either made as proposed, amended or abandoned. 3. Further information about the Order may be obtained by telephoning Housing Services on 020 3475 2314 or online at https://communityconversations.royalgreenwich.gov.uk/statutory-consultation-housing-estate-parking-restrictions 4. The Order and other documents giving more detailed particulars of the Order are available for inspection during normal office hours until the end of six weeks from the date on which the Order was made, at Housing Services, Royal Borough of Greenwich, The Woolwich Centre, 35 Wellington Street, SE18 6HQ or online at https://communityconversations.royalgreenwich.gov.uk/statutory-consultation-housing-estate-parking-restrictions 5. If any person wishes to question the validity of the Order or of any of the provisions contained therein on the grounds that they are not within the powers conferred by the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, or that any requirement of that Act or of any instrument made under that Act has not been complied with, that person may, within six weeks from the date on which the Order was made, apply for that purpose to the High Court. NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham made the above-mentioned Order under the powers granted by sections 9 and 10 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 as amended. The Order will come into force on 08th December 2026 and may continue in force for up to 18 months. 2. The general effect of the above-mentioned Order will be to prohibit any motor vehicle from proceeding past points in Margravine Gardens, at a point outside No. 16 Margravine Gardens and in Margravine Road, at a point in line with the south-eastern corner of No. 42 Margravine Road. 3. The controls specified in article 2 would not apply in respect of a vehicle – (a) with a valid permit; (b) being a taxi and pedal cycle; (c) in the pursuance of any statutory duty of the Post Office for the purpose of collecting or delivering letters provided the vehicle bears the Royal Mail livery; (d) being used in connection with building operations or demolition works near or adjacent to the restriction; (e) being used in connection with the maintenance, improvement, reconstruction, cleansing or lighting of a road; (f) being used in connection with the laying, erection, alteration or repair in or near or adjacent to the restriction of any sewer or of any main, pipe or apparatus for the supply of gas, water or electricity, or of any telecommunications apparatus as defined in paragraph 1(1) of Schedule 2 of the Telecommunications Act 1984; (g) if it is being used for ambulance, fire brigade or police purposes. 4. The Council will consider in due course whether the provisions of the Order should be continued in force indefinitely by means of permanent Order made under sections 6, 45 and 46 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984. Any person may object to the making of the permanent Order within a period of six months beginning with the date on which the experimental Order come into force or, if the Order is varied by another Order or modified pursuant to section 10(2) of the 1984 Act, beginning with the date on which the variation or modification or the latest variation or modification comes into force. The general effect of the Order will be as an experiment to: 1. Replace the existing ‘Resident Permit Holders Only Zone CH1 Mon-Fri 8.30am-5.30pm’ bays with ‘Payment Parking (TC2) Mon-Fri 8.30am-5.30pm Max stay 4hrs No return within 2hrs and Resident Permit Holders Only Zone CH1 Mon-Fri 8.30am-5.30pm’ bays on Seabrook Road at the following locations: a. North side, adjacent to No. 408 Valence Avenue. b. South side, adjacent to No. 410 Valence Avenue. 2. Replace the existing ‘Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm 1hr No return within 4hrs’ bays with ‘Payment Parking (TC2) Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm Max stay 4hrs No return within 2hrs’ bays on Becontree Avenue at the following locations: a. North side, outside Nos. 453 to 457 Becontree Avenue. b. South side, outside Nos. 460 to 464 Becontree Avenue. 3. Replace the existing ‘Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm 1hr No return within 2hrs’ bay with a ‘Payment Parking (TC2) Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm Max stay 4hrs No return within 2hrs’ bay on Becontree Avenue, north side, outside No. 427 to 439 Becontree Avenue. 4. Replace the existing ‘Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm 1hr No return within 2hrs’ and ‘Electric Vehicle Charging Only Max stay 4hrs No return within 2hrs’ bays with ‘Payment Parking (TC2) Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm Max stay 4hrs No return within 2hrs’ bays on Becontree Avenue, south side, outside Nos. 434 to 444 Becontree Avenue. 5. Replace the existing ‘No waiting Mon-Fri 8.30am-5.30pm’ restriction and ‘Resident Permit Holders Only Zone CH1 Mon-Fri 8.30am-5.30pm’ bay with ‘Payment Parking (TC2) Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm Max stay 4hrs No return within 2hrs’ bays on Becontree Avenue, north side, from a point 4 metres west of the common boundary of Nos. 384 and 386 Becontree Avenue for 30.8 metres in a westerly direction. A copy of all scheme documents including the Experimental Traffic Orders, which will come into force on 2nd December 2026, a statement of the Council’s reasons for the scheme, along with scheme plans, are available to view on the Councils website by visiting the following web page https://www.lbbd.gov.uk/parking/parking-area and selecting ‘New and proposed traffic and parking schemes’ or available for inspection at the Adult Library, First Floor, Barking Learning Centre, Barking between the hours of 9.00am and 4.00pm Monday to Friday. The Order provides that in pursuance of section 10(2) of the Act, the specified officer may, if it appears essential in the interests of the expeditious, convenient and safe movement of traffic on the highway or for preserving or improving the amenities of the area through which any road affected by the Order runs, modify or suspend the Order or any of its provisions. If the Orders are varied by other Orders, a further consultation period will commence beginning with the day on which the latest variation or modification comes into operation. Further details will be provided, if required. The Order is to be on an experimental basis for a maximum period of 18 months and the Council will be considering in due course whether the provisions of the Order should be continued in force indefinitely by means of permanent Order made under sections 6, 45, 46, 49, 122 (1) and (2) and 124 and Parts I to IV of the Act, as amended. Any person may object to the making of the permanent Order for the purpose of such indefinite continuation within a period of six months beginning with the day on which the above-mentioned Order came into operation with the deadline for representations being 2nd June 2027. Representations to this scheme must be made in writing and must state the grounds on which it is made and be sent for the attention of Sarah Marriott-Carle to the address below or to https://www.lbbd.gov.uk/form/tmo-feedback, quoting ref 10739 – BecontreeAve&SeabrookRd. Any objection may be communicated to other persons who may be affected. Dated 25th November 2026 Tina Brooks, Head of Parking Services, Enforcement Services, Town Hall, Barking, Essex IG11 7LU Actions Save notice to My Gazette Remove from My Gazette Loading... The general effect of the Order would be to amend the waiting and loading restrictions at the junction in Bourne Hill, Green Lanes, and Hedge Lane. The amendments are being proposed in conjunction with minor improvements to the existing cycle infrastructure at the Bourne Hill / Green Lanes / Hedge Lane junction. 2. NOTICE IS ALSO HEREBY GIVEN that the Council, in accordance with sections 65 and 66 of the Highways Act 1980, and under section 23 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, intends to:- a) alter the four existing signalised pedestrian crossings at the junction of Bourne Hill, Green Lanes and Hedge Lane by making provision for pedal cycles to use them; b) establish a new crossing for pedestrians and pedal cycles in the Hedge Lane slip-road, to be located between the south-eastern kerb-line of Green Lanes and the bus stand (the existing bus stand on the Hedge Lane slip-road would be relocated southward by approximately 3 metres); c) in Green Lanes, on both sides, introduce segregated cycle tracks on the existing cycle lane network within the footway on either side of the Bourne Hill/ Hedge Lane junction; d) create a shared area for pedestrian footway and cycle track on:- (i) Bourne Hill, the southwest side; and (ii) Hedge Lane slip road, the south-east side between Green Lanes and the main arm of Hedge Lane. 3. A copy of the proposed Order, the Notice and of the Council’s Statement of Reasons for proposing to make the Order can:- (a) be inspected at the Town Library, 66 Church Street, Enfield EN2 6AX, Monday to Fridays 9am – 5pm inclusive; (b) also be inspected online at: https://new.enfield.gov.uk/services/roads-and-transport/traffic-management-orders/ (c) be obtained by emailing [contact removed] or by writing to Transport, Climate and Place (quoting reference TG52/1622 Civic Centre, Silver Street, Enfield, Middlesex, EN1 3XA. 4. Any person desiring to object to the proposed Order, or make any other representations in respect of it should send a statement in writing to that effect, and in the case of an objection stating the grounds thereof, to Journey and Places, the Civic Centre, Silver Street, Enfield, Middlesex, EN1 3XD by 16th December 2026 or by e-mail to [contact removed] Dated 25th November 2026 Hussain Rab, Head of Design and Construction Actions Save notice to My Gazette Remove from My Gazette Loading... Final Date For Submission: 24 December 2026. Notice is hereby given, pursuant to Rule 14.28 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016, that the liquidator of the Company named above (in members’ voluntary liquidation) intends to make final distributions to creditors. Creditors are required to prove their debts on or before the final date for submission specified in this notice by sending full details of their claims to the liquidator. Creditors must also, if so requested by the liquidator, provide such further details and documentary evidence to support their claims as the liquidator deems necessary. The intended distributions are final distributions and may be made without regard to any claims not proved by the final date for submission specified in this notice. Any creditor who has not proved their debt by that date, or who increases the claim in their proof after that date, will not be entitled to disturb the intended final distributions. The liquidator intends that, after paying or providing for final distributions in respect of creditors who have proved their claims, all funds remaining in the liquidator’s hands following the final distributions to creditors shall be distributed to the shareholders of the Company absolutely. The directors have made a statutory declaration that the Company is able to pay all their known liabilities in full. Date of Appointment: 16 November 2026 Liquidator's Name and Address: James Hopkirk (IP No. 21150) of Kreston Reeves LLP, 2nd Floor Maritime Place, Quayside, Chatham Maritime, Kent, ME4 4QZ. text: Julian Blazeby appointed Chairman of the Disclosure and Barring Service | Julian Blazeby has been appointed as the new Chairman of the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS). He joined the DBS Board in April 2023 and has been Vice Chairman since April. Julian served as a police officer for 30 years in 3 different forces. He retired as an Assistant Chief Constable in Staffordshire in 2014 before going on to hold the role of Deputy Chief of Police in Jersey between 2017 to 2018. He has also held senior civil service roles in the Ministry of Defence and the Independent Police Complaints Commission and was a Director General in the Government of Jersey where he led the Justice and Home Affairs Department. Julian is also the Independent Chair of the Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority. Julian succeeds Dr Gillian Fairfield, whose 8-year tenure as Chairman ends on 30 November 2026. His appointment follows a robust competition in accordance with the requirements of the Governance Code of Public Appointments. He will begin his tenure on 1 December 2026. Julian Blazeby said: I am honoured to be appointed as Chairman of the Disclosure and Barring Service. DBS plays a vital role in helping employers make safer recruitment decisions, and I look forward to continuing to work with the Board, the executive team and colleagues across DBS to build on the strong foundations Dr Gillian Fairfield has laid.
title: Julian Blazeby appointed Chairman of the Disclosure and Barring Service

text: Professor Danielle George CBE appointed Trustee to the Science Museum Group | Professor Danielle George CBE Appointed from 01 February 2027 to 31 January 2031. Danielle George has been Professor of Radio Frequency Engineering at the University of Manchester since 2014 and has been the Government’s Chief Scientific Adviser for National Security since 2025. In 2020/21 she served as President of the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET) and as Vice President of the British Computer Society. In 2016, she was appointed MBE for services to engineering through public engagement and received the Royal Academy of Engineering’s Rooke Medal. In 2017, she was awarded the Harold Hartley Medal for her contribution to Measurement and Control. In 2024, she was appointed CBE in The King’s New Year Honours. Remuneration and Governance Code Trustees of the Science Museum Group are not remunerated. This appointment has been made in accordance with the Governance Code on Public Appointments . The appointments process is regulated by the Commissioner for Public Appointments . Under the Code, any significant political activity undertaken by an appointee in the last five years must be declared. This is defined as including holding office, public speaking, making a recordable donation, or candidature for election. Danielle George has declared no political activity. Notes to Editors DCMS has around 463 regulated Public Appointment roles across 44 Public Bodies including Arts Council England, Theatres Trust, the National Gallery, UK Sport and the Gambling Commission. We encourage applications from talented individuals from all backgrounds and across the whole of the United Kingdom. To find out more about Public Appointments or to apply visit the HM Government Public Appointments Website .
title: Professor Danielle George CBE appointed Trustee to the Science Museum Group

text: Ravi Mahendra appointed Non-Executive Director at HM Courts and Tribunals Service | Ravi Mahendra has joined the HMCTS Board, bringing more than 25 years’ experience in governance, risk, assurance, finance and operational delivery. Ravi joined HMCTS as a non-executive director and member of its Audit and Risk Assurance Committee (ARAC) on 1 November 2026. He has more than 25 years’ experience in governance, risk, assurance, finance and operational delivery. He has held senior leadership roles at Marsh McLennan, AIG, subsidiaries of GE Capital and at PwC. He has experience as Audit and Risk Committee Chair at East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust and as an Audit and Risk Committee member at Goldsmiths, University of London. His experience spans financial services, healthcare, higher education and the charitable sector. Sir Richard Broadbent, Chair of the HMCTS Board, said: “I am delighted to welcome Ravi to the HMCTS Board. He joins a strong non-executive team, bringing his experience in governance, audit, risk and financial management in challenging environments, alongside a strong understanding of operational delivery.” Non-executive director reappointments HMCTS has also confirmed the reappointment of Nick Fishwick and Luisa Fulci as non-executive directors for second three-year terms, from 1 January 2027 and 1 April 2027 respectively. Nick became Chair of ARAC on 1 November 2026, while Luisa will continue to chair the HMCTS Business Review Committee. The role of our non-executive directors The HMCTS Board provides leadership and direction to the organisation. Non-executive directors provide independent advice, scrutiny and challenge, contribute to the Board’s oversight of strategy and performance, and support effective corporate governance and risk management.
title: Ravi Mahendra appointed Non-Executive Director at HM Courts and Tribunals Service

She was formerly a senior curator of the British Museum’s Anglo-Saxon, late Celtic and Viking collections and Keeper of the Department of Britain, Europe and Prehistory. She has served as an Honorary Visiting Professor at the Institute of Archaeology, University College London, and as President of the Society for Medieval Archaeology and is a Fellow of the Society of Antiquaries. She has lectured and published widely. Her recent books include Anglo-Saxon Art: A New History (2012), The Franks Casket (2012), and, as co-editor and contributor, The Staffordshire Hoard: an Anglo-Saxon Treasure (2019). text: Professor Jackline Wahba OBE appointed Chair of the Migration Advisory Committee | Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has welcomed Professor Jackline Wahba OBE to her new role as chair of the MAC. The MAC is an independent non-departmental public body that advises the government on the immigration system. It is sponsored by the Home Office. Professor Wahba takes over as full-time chair from Dr Madeleine Sumption, who has been interim chair since March 2026. She has been appointed for a 3-year term to November 2029. Dr Sumption will return to her term as deputy chair. Professor Wahba was appointed after an open and fair recruitment process. This followed the Governance Code on Public Appointments, the process for which is regulated by the Commissioner for Public Appointments The MAC carries out research and analysis on migration. It has worked with Skills England, the Department for Work and Pensions and the Industrial Strategy Council. Together they have developed an evidence-based approach to building up the homegrown workforce and reducing reliance on international recruitment. Net migration under this government has fallen by 74%. Last year, the government kept its manifesto promise on the MAC by giving it more money and staff . This lets the committee forecast future migration trends and make policy recommendations more strategically. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: I welcome Professor Wahba’s appointment and look forward to working with the committee as it continues to provide expert advice on migration issues. Our approach to migration policy must be based on thorough, factual analysis. That is why this government has given the MAC the resources it needs to make timely, evidence-based recommendations. Chair of the MAC, Professor Jackline Wahba OBE said: I am delighted to have been appointed Chair of the Migration Advisory Committee. The MAC plays an important role in providing independent, evidence-based advice to government on migration and its impacts on the UK economy and labour market. I look forward to building on the MAC’s important work and ensuring that our advice continues to be informed by rigorous research and robust evidence. Professor Wahba is a Professor of Economics at the University of Southampton. She is a leading economist, and her research focuses on the economics of international migration and refugees. She was awarded an OBE for services to economic policy in 2020. She has advised governments and international organisations, including the World Bank, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, the International Labour Organisation and the European Commission.
title: Professor Jackline Wahba OBE appointed Chair of the Migration Advisory Committee

text: Mr Justice Pepperall appointed Chair of the Law Commission of England and Wales | The Lord Chancellor and Secretary of State for Justice has approved the appointment of The Honourable Mr Justice Pepperall as the Chair of the Law Commission for England and Wales for 3 years from 1 January 2027. The Law Commission is the statutory independent body created by the Law Commissions Act 1965 to keep the law of England and Wales under review and to recommend reform where it is needed. The aim of the Commission is to ensure that the law is fair, modern, simple and cost effective. The Chair of the Law Commission is appointed, by the Lord Chancellor, under Section 1 of the Law Commissions Act 1965. Biography Sir Edward (Ed) Pepperall is a High Court Judge of the King’s Bench Division authorised to sit in the Technology & Construction Court, the Media & Communications List, the Administrative Court, the Planning Court, and in homicide and terrorism work in the Crown Court. Appointed to the High Court in 2018, he served as Presiding Judge on the Midland Circuit between 2020 and 2023. He served on the Civil Procedure Rule Committee between 2010 and 2016 and again from 2024 as well as on the Civil Judicial Engagement Group, the Civil Executive Team and the Contempt Procedure Rules Working Group.
title: Mr Justice Pepperall appointed Chair of the Law Commission of England and Wales

text: Alan Milburn appointed Chair of the Youth Opportunities Unit | Alan Milburn has been appointed as the Chair of the new Youth Opportunities Unit. The new Unit will sit at the centre of government, reporting directly to the Prime Minister, driving the cross-system changes needed to deliver greater opportunities and support for young people. The appointment follows the publication of the independent Milburn Report into young people and work. The report identified a lack of coordination between government and between central and local government and other partners on the challenges facing young people out of work, education or training. The Unit will address this, working between government departments and with local government and other partners. The responsibilities of the new Unit are to: Shaping and delivering the Government response: Shaping and delivering the cross-government response to the Milburn Review, maintaining an ambitious cross-system approach to reform and linking closely to the Government’s wider agenda on growth, re-industrialisation and devolution. Unblocking delivery and driving progress: Unblocking delivery obstacles and supporting Secretaries of State to drive progress towards reducing NEET rates. Guarantee, service design and devolution: Driving delivery of the Youth Opportunity and Support Guarantee and the Youth Opportunities Service, partnering with Number 10 North, departments, Mayors, Strategic and Local Authorities. Mobilising partners: Galvanising action beyond central government, working with Mayors, securing commitments from employers and voluntary and community organisations, and demonstrating progress. Data, metrics and insight: Drawing on data and insight to understand what is and is not working, and addressing gaps in, or barriers to, data sharing to aid delivery. The terms of reference for the Youth Opportunities Unit are published online. ENDS
title: Alan Milburn appointed Chair of the Youth Opportunities Unit

text: Rupert Jones appointed Independent Reviewer of Terrorism and State Threats Legislation | Former judge Rupert Jones has been appointed as the government’s new Independent Reviewer of Terrorism Legislation and Independent Reviewer of State Threats Legislation. He succeeds Jonathan Hall KC, who has served as both reviewers since May 2019 and February 2024, respectively. Rupert has had a distinguished career as a barrister and judge, specialising in areas including proceeds of crime and national security. In addition to appearing as counsel in cases before the House of Lords, Supreme Court, and Privy Council, he was a judge of the Upper Tribunal, authorised to sit as a judge of the High Court, and a legal member of the Investigatory Powers Tribunal. Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, said: The threats we face from terrorism and foreign states are growing. So, it is vital we have the best independent and expert scrutiny of the powers we use to keep the public safe. Rupert’s deep legal expertise and sound judgement will be vital in ensuring our response remains effective and proportionate. I would also like to pay tribute to Jonathan Hall for his long and distinguished service in the role. His rigorous oversight and analysis have improved our laws and made our country safer. Rupert Jones said: I am very grateful to have been given the opportunity to serve in this role and provide an independent contribution to an evolving area of the law which is of significant public importance. When reviewing the operation of the relevant provisions, I hope to inform public debate, scrutinise the use of the legislation and make appropriate recommendations, paying due regard to fairness and effectiveness, liberty and security. During his tenure, Jonathan Hall KC has made a significant contribution to the development and scrutiny of the UK’s counter-terrorism and national security framework. Notably, he helped shape the government’s approach to youth diversion orders, introduced in response to the growing number of young people involved in counter-terrorism casework. More recently, as the first Independent Reviewer of State Threats Legislation, his recommendation led to the introduction of proscription-like powers for the Home Secretary to designate state linked organisations involved in hostile activity against the UK. Jonathan Hall KC said: The independent reviewer carries out a unique and, I believe, an important role. I am very grateful to all the members of the public, officials, police, civil society organisations, academics, journalists, Parliamentarians, and ministers who gave up time, information and expertise to allow me to review how national security laws operate in practice. After more than seven years as independent reviewer, it is time for a fresh pair of eyes, and I wish Rupert Jones every success. Both roles are responsible for assessing the fairness, effectiveness and proportionality of UK state threats and terrorism legislation, acting as important oversight and scrutiny. The reviewer is required to provide separate annual reports covering both pieces of legislation, of which their findings and recommendations will be reported to Parliament. Rupert Jones will also be appointed to carry out future reviews for the Treasury and Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, as required under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018, a role that Jonathan Hall KC had previously been appointed to, and delivered a report under in December 2023. His appointment follows a robust competition in accordance with the requirements of the Governance Code of Public Appointments. He will begin his tenure on 23 November 2026.
title: Rupert Jones appointed Independent Reviewer of Terrorism and State Threats Legislation

text: Shellie Adams reappointed as a member of the Parole Board | The Lord Chancellor and Secretary of State for Justice has approved the reappointment of a Parole Board member. Shellie Adams will be reappointed for a further term of 5-years from 1 February 2027 until 31 January 2032. Parole Board members are appointed, by ministers, under Schedule 19 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003. The appointment of Parole Board members - save for judicial members - is regulated by the Commissioner for Public Appointments (CPA). Recruitment processes comply with the Governance Code on Public Appointments. The Parole Board is an independent body that works with its criminal justice partners to protect the public by risk assessing prisoners to decide whether they can be safely released into the community. The Parole Board was established by the Criminal Justice Act 1967. It is an executive Non-Departmental Public Body sponsored by the Ministry of Justice.
title: Shellie Adams reappointed as a member of the Parole Board
