text: Luke Jensen appointed Chair of the National Savings and Investments Board | The Minister for Pensions announced today (4 November 2026) that Luke Jensen has been appointed as the Chair to the National Savings and Investments (NS&I) Board, following a fair and open competition run by HM Treasury. Luke’s three-year term began on 2 November 2026. Luke has sat on the NS&I Board since 1 April 2024 and was Interim Chair following Lord Gerard Lemos CMG CBE stepping down as Chair in July 2025, following his appointment to the Whip’s Office within the House of Lords. Luke brings a wealth of experience to the role from his senior executive and non-executive career across a range of retail and consumer-focused environments. Luke is currently a non-executive director for the Co-operative Group and a Senior Advisor to the Board at Eat Happy Hana Group. The Minister for Pensions said: I am pleased to appoint Luke Jensen as Chair of the NS&I Board, strengthening the organisation’s leadership and oversight. Luke will continue to support NS&I in providing cost-effective finance for the Government, progressing its remediation scheme following its recent bereavement claims issue, and driving forward its transformation programme. NS&I Interim Chief Executive, Sir Jim Harra, said: I welcome Luke Jensen’s appointment as NS&I’s new Chair. He has the experience and leadership to ensure that NS&I remains a vital source of government funding and a key part of the UK savings market. Further information Luke Jensen’s appointment was regulated by the Office of the Commissioner for Public Appointments (OCPA) and conducted under fair and open competition in accordance with the Cabinet Office’s Governance Code on Public Appointments . Under the Code, any political activity undertaken by an appointee in the last five years must be declared. This is defined as including holding office, public speaking, making a recordable donation, or candidature for election. Luke Jensen has not declared any political activity. Non-executive members of NS&I’s Board ensure a sound strategy is in place to meet the organisation’s remit of raising cost-effective debt financing for the government. They also act as an external source of advice, have oversight of risk control and ensure NS&I’s links with its outsourcing partners remain open and transparent. NS&I is one of the largest savings organisations in the UK, offering a range of savings and investments. All products offer 100% security because NS&I is backed by HM Treasury.
title: Luke Jensen appointed Chair of the National Savings and Investments Board

text: Dr Ewan Kirk appointed MOD Director Innovation | Dr Ewan Kirk has been appointed the MOD’s new Director Innovation. He will lead UK Defence Innovation (UKDI), part of the newly designed National Armaments (NA) Innovation area which sits under Director General Innovation Anthony Reeves . NA Innovation brings together some 4,800 experts and scientists in UKDI , the Defence Investment Unit, the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl) and the Defence Uncrewed Systems Centre (DUSC). It has a ringfenced £1.6 billion defence innovation budget over the next four years (UKDI), as well as supporting £2.1 billion of investment in core science and technology. Led by Dr Kirk, UKDI will support the NAD Group’s commitments under the Strategic Defence Review, including delivering innovative capability at rapid pace and creating economic growth through increased production, export opportunities and jobs, while ensuring innovation remains at the heart of UK military capability. With UKDI being the single point of contact for industry to engage with defence on innovation challenges and opportunities, Dr Kirk will build relationships with the UK’s technology sector, venture capitalists and private equity investors. His other responsibilities will include fostering close relations on innovation and capability development with the RAF’s Rapid Capabilities Office, Royal Navy’s Disruptive Capabilities and Technologies Office (DCTO), British Army’s Rapstone and Cyber & Specialist Operations Command’s jHub. Rupert Pearce, the National Armaments Director , said: Ewan’s appointment is a significant step in making innovation central to how Defence delivers for our Armed Forces, one of the pillars of the SDR. UKDI gives industry, investors and academia a single front door to work with us, and Ewan has the scientific depth and commercial experience to make that real. If we can leverage the extraordinary inventiveness of the UK economy, Defence can gain sustained capability advantage over its adversaries, providing us with enhanced deterrence. Working alongside Anthony Reeves and the wider National Armaments Innovation team, Ewan will help us deliver innovative defence capability quickly, keep our Armed Forces ahead of their adversaries and turn defence innovation into jobs, exports and growth across the UK. Dr Kirk was a Non-Executive Director of BAE Systems, Chairman of DeepTech Labs and Chairman of the Management Committee of the Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences. Commenting on his appointment, Dr Kirk said: Innovation thrives when the best ideas can move quickly from the lab to the front line. I’m delighted to join the National Armaments Director Group and look forward to working with Rupert, with Anthony Reeves, the UK’s technology sector, investors, academia and our NATO allies to bring cutting-edge technologies, such as artificial intelligence and cyber, into military service as quickly we can. Since UKDI was formed in early 2025, John Cunningham has led the organisation as interim director, building UKDI from a concept into an operational organisation embedded within the NAD Group. During this time, UKDI has delivered innovative capability to the front line, strengthened the national innovation ecosystem across all stakeholders, built a portfolio of exciting projects and created the strong foundations for UKDI’s next phase of growth and impact. This appointment of the new UKDI Director directly supports the UK Armed Forces, keeping their war-fighting advantage while promoting national prosperity through defence and dual-use technologies, such as artificial intelligence and cyber, and through private investment.
title: Dr Ewan Kirk appointed MOD Director Innovation

text: Raj Jethwa reappointed as a member of the Prison Service Pay Review Body | The Lord Chancellor and Secretary of State for Justice has approved the reappointment of Raj Jethwa for a second term from 13 June 2027 to 12 June 2032. The PSPRB provides the government with independent advice on the remuneration of operational prison staff in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, as set out in The Prison Service (Pay Review Body) Regulations 2001 (SI 2001 No. 1161). Appointments and re-appointments to the PSPRB are regulated by the Commissioner for Public Appointments. Appointments and Reappointments comply with the Cabinet Office Governance Code on Public Appointments. Public appointments to the PSPRB are made by the Prime Minister. Biography Raj Jethwa is currently Chief Executive of the Universities and Colleges Employers Association (UCEA), representing the UK higher education sector in all employment matters and in collective negotiations on pay, pensions and related issues. Raj was previously the Director of Policy at the British Medical Association (BMA) where he led its professional activities, policy development and collective bargaining functions. Raj has also worked as Head of Research for the Police Federation of England and Wales and as a policy advisor at the Trades Union Congress (TUC). He has declared no political activity.
title: Raj Jethwa reappointed as a member of the Prison Service Pay Review Body

text: Major-General Lisa Keetley appointed Army Trustee to the Imperial War Museum Board | Major-General Lisa Keetley Major-General Lisa Keetley has been appointed for a term of four years on the Imperial War Museum Board, commencing on 1 November 2026. Major-General Keetley is currently serving as the Defence Services Secretary in the Ministry of Defence. Following her commissioning into the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers from the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, she worked across the British Army, Defence and NATO. Her operational service has included deployments to Bosnia, Iraq and Afghanistan. Most recently, she served as Commander of the International Donor Coordination Centre and Deputy Commanding General (Support) of the Security Assistance Group Ukraine, coordinating international military assistance in support of Ukraine. She is the Founder of the Army Service Women’s Network and has been a longstanding advocate for the advancement of women across Defence. Remuneration and Governance Code Trustees of the Imperial War Museum are not remunerated. This appointment has been made in accordance with the Governance Code on Public Appointments . The appointments process is regulated by the Commissioner for Public Appointments . Under the Code, any significant political activity undertaken by an appointee in the last five years must be declared. This is defined as including holding office, public speaking, making a recordable donation, or candidature for election. Major-General Lisa Keetley has not declared any such political activity. title: Major-General Lisa Keetley appointed Army Trustee to the Imperial War Museum Board

text: Sir Nicholas Coleridge CBE reappointed as Chair of Historic Royal Palaces | Sir Nicholas Coleridge Sir Nicholas Coleridge CBE was first appointed as Chair of Historic Royal Palaces in November 2023. He has been Chair of The King’s Foundation since 2026. Previously, he was Chair of the Victoria and Albert Museum from 2015 to 2023. He was successively Editorial Director, Managing Director and President of the Condé Nast media group over a thirty-year period. He has been Chair of the Professional Publishers Association, Chair of the British Fashion Council, Chair of the Prince of Wales’ Campaign for Wool, and was Co-Chair of the late Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee Pageant. He is the author of fifteen books, both fiction and non-fiction. Remuneration and Governance Code The Chair of Historic Royal Palaces is not remunerated. This appointment has been made in accordance with the Cabinet Office’s Governance Code on Public Appointments . The appointments process is regulated by the Commissioner for Public Appointments. Under the Code, any significant political activity undertaken by an appointee in the last five years must be declared. This is defined as including holding office, public speaking, making a recordable donation, or candidature for election. Sir Nicholas Coleridge has donated to the Conservative and Unionist Party in the last five years.
title: Sir Nicholas Coleridge CBE reappointed as Chair of Historic Royal Palaces
